mainTopic: זוגות — the danger of pairs: its source, who is affected, its limits, and which cups count together
overview: This amud opens with the end of a counter-spell against witches. The גמרא then discusses זוגות, the danger of doing things in pairs. In ארץ ישראל people were not careful about pairs, but רב דימי מנהרדעא was, and his barrel burst. The rule is that whoever is careful about pairs is affected by them, though everyone should still be somewhat cautious. רב דימי reports that four items in pairs are a הלכה למשה מסיני. Since one of the four is unknown, the רבנן forbade all pairs. Larger even numbers are safe from מזיקין but not from כשפים, as the story of the man who died after losing count at sixteen cups shows. The גמרא then limits the concern: things finished by people, a store, a guest, someone who changed his mind, and an ordinary woman are exempt. It closes with rules for which cups count together: אִיסְפָּרָגוֹס, wine with beer, cups before and during the meal (debated by רב משרשיא), and finally diluted drinks, a rule that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the counter-spell against the witches
steps.stepSummary: The closing words of the incantation a person says when meeting witches: may your magic ingredients scatter, and may your power over me be gone.
steps.simpleTranslation: Your spices should scatter. The wind should carry away the fresh saffron that you witches hold. As long as I was favored from Heaven and you showed me favor, I did not come here. Now that I have come here, your favor toward me has cooled, and you should find favor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a protective incantation that it began earlier. A person says it to cancel the power of witches (נשים כשפניות).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The spell attacks the tools of the כשפים, which are the spices and the saffron used in witchcraft, and asks that the wind scatter them. The second half plays on the word חן, favor, to say the witches no longer have any hold over the speaker.

keyTerms.meaning: I was shown favor (wordplay on חן)

phrases.english: May your spices be scattered,
phrases.notes: The spices used for witchcraft

phrases.english: may the wind carry away the fresh saffron
that you hold, you witch women,
As long as I was favored (from Heaven) and you showed me favor,
I did not come in here.
Now that I have come in here,
your favor toward me has cooled, and you should find favor.
phrases.notes: End of the incantation

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues and completes the incantation earlier
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The wording of the protective incantation against witches

steps.title: In the Land of Israel people were not careful about pairs
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reports that in ארץ ישראל people did not worry about זוגות at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the West, meaning ארץ ישראל, they were not particular about pairs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the topic of זוגות and gives a fact: in ארץ ישראל nobody worried about it. This sets up the contrast with רב דימי in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the סוגיא has treated pairs as a real danger. This line shows that the concern was not shared everywhere, which prepares the ground for the rule in step 4 that the danger depends on whether a person is careful about it.

keyTerms.meaning: in the West, meaning ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: In the West they were not particular about pairs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the incantation and returns to the general topic of זוגות
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In ארץ ישראל people were not concerned about זוגות

steps.title: רב דימי מנהרדעא was careful even about barrel marks, and a barrel burst
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי מנהרדעא was extremely careful about pairs, even with symbols on barrels. Once there were pairs of marks on a barrel, and it burst.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב דימי from נהרדעא was particular even about the marks on a barrel. There was an incident, and the barrel burst.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the opposite example: a sage who was very careful about pairs. It then tells a story showing that, for him, the danger was real.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the reverse of step 2. For someone who is careful, even a small thing like a pair of marks on a barrel caused damage. The two cases together lead straight into the rule in step 4.
steps.confusionAlert: This רב דימי מנהרדעא is a Babylonian sage. He is not the same person as the רב דימי in step 5, who brought teachings from ארץ ישראל to בבל.

phrases.english: Rav Dimi from Neharde'a
was particular even about the marks on a barrel.
There was an incident, and the barrel burst.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite case to the people of ארץ ישראל
steps.raayaObject: That זוגות can cause real damage to someone who is careful about them
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of רב דימי's barrel bursting

steps.title: The rule: whoever is careful is affected, but everyone should still be cautious
steps.stepSummary: Whoever is particular about pairs, the harmful forces are particular with him. Whoever is not particular, they leave him alone. Even so, a person should be somewhat concerned.
steps.simpleTranslation: The rule of the matter is this: whoever is particular, they are particular with him. Whoever is not particular, they are not particular with him. However, one still needs to be concerned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings steps 2 and 3 together into one general rule about who is affected by זוגות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The danger depends on the person's own attitude. That explains why ארץ ישראל was safe and רב דימי's barrel was not. The closing words ומיהו למיחש מיבעי add that a person should still not deliberately do things in pairs.

keyTerms.meaning: the general rule of the matter

steps.whatToRemember: With זוגות, the more a person worries about it, the more it affects him. Still, a person should avoid doing things in pairs on purpose.

phrases.english: The rule of the matter:
whoever is particular, they are particular with him;
phrases.notes: "They" means the demons or harmful forces

phrases.english: and whoever is not particular, they are not particular with him.
However, one still needs to be concerned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Combines the two opposite cases into one rule
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The danger of זוגות follows the person's own concern, but some caution is always needed

steps.title: רב דימי's report: four pairs are a law given to Moses at Sinai
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי, arriving from ארץ ישראל, taught that two eggs, two nuts, two cucumbers, and one other item are dangerous in pairs, and that this is a הלכה למשה מסיני.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came from ארץ ישראל, he said: two eggs, two nuts, two cucumbers, and another matter are a הלכה למשה מסיני.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי brings a teaching from ארץ ישראל that gives a very strong source for the concern about pairs: a tradition going back to Sinai.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This raises the level of authority. The concern is no longer just custom or experience. For these specific four items it is a הלכה למשה מסיני. However, the fourth item is not named.

keyTerms.meaning: when he came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)
a law passed down orally from משה at Sinai

steps.confusionAlert: Step 2 said that in ארץ ישראל people were not careful about pairs. This teaching also comes from ארץ ישראל. The tradition from Sinai itself names only these specific items. Step 6 explains how the רבנן then extended the concern to all pairs.

phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came, he said:
two eggs, and two nuts,
two cucumbers, and another matter —
are a halakha transmitted to Moses from Sinai.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from experience and custom to the halachic source of the concern
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two eggs, two nuts, two cucumbers, and one other item in pairs are forbidden by הלכה למשה מסיני

steps.title: Because the fourth item is unknown, the רבנן forbade all pairs
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן did not know what the דבר אחר was, so they made a גזירה against all pairs to be safe.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן were uncertain what the other matter is, so the רבנן decreed against all pairs because of that other matter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the concern spreads beyond the three named items. Since nobody knew the fourth item, the רבנן covered every pair.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban on all pairs is a rabbinic גזירה built around a Sinaitic core. Only four items are truly from Sinai, but since one is unknown, the רבנן made a wide fence so that nobody would accidentally violate the real law.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the two layers of זוגות: a small core from Sinai, and a wide rabbinic גזירה covering everything else because of the doubt.

phrases.english: And the Sages were uncertain
what the other matter is,
so the Sages decreed against all pairs
because of the other matter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the limited Sinaitic law grew into a ban on all pairs
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because the fourth item is unknown, the רבנן forbade all pairs

steps.title: Larger even numbers are safe only from demons, not from witchcraft
steps.stepSummary: The earlier statement that ten, eight, six, and four are not a problem of pairs applies only to מזיקין. With כשפים, even larger numbers are a concern.
steps.simpleTranslation: What we said, that ten, eight, six, and four have no problem of pairs, applies only to harmful spirits. But regarding witchcraft, we are concerned even about larger numbers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a rule stated earlier in the סוגיא and limits it. The safety of those even numbers protects only against demons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the גמרא said that bigger even numbers do not count as זוגות. Here it clarifies that this exception works only against מזיקין. Witchcraft can still use even numbers above two, so for כשפים the concern remains even with many items.

keyTerms.meaning: and that which we said (referring back to an earlier statement)

steps.whatToRemember: There are two different dangers. For מזיקין, only small pairs are a problem, and ten, eight, six, and four are fine. For כשפים, even larger even numbers can be a concern.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as cancelling the earlier rule. Ten, eight, six, and four are still safe from מזיקין. The exception just does not carry over to כשפים.

phrases.english: And that which we said,
ten, eight, six, four
do not involve the problem of pairs,
we said only regarding harmful spirits.
But regarding witchcraft,
even with many we are also concerned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to an earlier rule in the סוגיא about larger even numbers and limits it
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The safety of ten, eight, six, and four applies to מזיקין only. For כשפים, even larger numbers are still a concern.

steps.title: The story of the divorced man, the wine shop, and sixteen cups
steps.stepSummary: A man kept drinking at his ex-wife's husband's wine shop. Her כשפים could not hurt him because he guarded against pairs. One day he lost count after sixteen cups, left on an even number, and died.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like the story of a man who divorced his wife. She married a wine seller. Every day the first husband would go to that shop and drink wine. She kept trying כשפים on him, but it did not work, because he was careful about pairs. One day he drank a lot and did not know how much he drank. Until sixteen cups he was clear-headed and careful. After that he was not clear-headed and not careful, and she made him leave after an even number. As he walked, an Arab met him and said: 'This is a dead man walking here.' He went and hugged a palm tree. The palm tree dried out, and he burst.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story to prove the point it just made: with כשפים, even large even numbers are dangerous.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man was fine as long as he counted his cups, even past ten. He stayed safe all the way to sixteen. This shows that for כשפים, the 'big numbers are safe' rule does not protect you. Once he lost track and left on an even number, the כשפים took effect and killed him.

keyTerms.meaning: A shopkeeper. Here, a wine seller.
A pair, meaning an even number.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think he was safe at sixteen because it is a 'big number.' He was safe only because he was still counting and careful. Step 7 said that with כשפים even big numbers count, and this story proves exactly that.
steps.whyThisMatters: It turns the rule from Step 7 into a real case. Being careful protects a person, and once that care slips, the כשפים can act.

phrases.english: Like that incident of a certain man
who divorced his wife.
(She went and) married a shopkeeper.
phrases.notes: He sold wine in his shop.

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל יוֹמָא הֲוָה אָזֵיל וְשָׁתֵי חַמְרָא.
phrases.english: Every day he (the first husband) would go and drink wine.
phrases.notes: He drank in that same shop.

phrases.english: She would perform witchcraft on him
and it was not effective for her against him,
because he was careful about pairs.
One day he drank a lot,
and he did not know how much he drank.
Until sixteen (cups) he was clear-headed
and was careful with himself,
from here onward he was not clear-headed
and was not careful with himself,
she sent him out on a pair.
phrases.notes: He left after an even number of cups.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֲוָה אָזֵיל, גָּס בֵּיהּ הָהוּא טַיָּיעָא,
phrases.english: As he was walking, a certain Arab met him,

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: גַּבְרָא קְטִילָא הוּא דְּאָזֵיל הָכָא.
phrases.english: and said to him: It is a dead man who is walking here.
He went and hugged a palm tree,
the palm tree dried out, and he burst.
phrases.notes: The power of the כשפים dried out the tree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows Step 7 in action: with כשפים, even a large even number like sixteen is dangerous.
steps.raayaObject: Step 7's rule that with כשפים, even numbers above ten still carry the danger of pairs.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of the man whose ex-wife's כשפים failed until he lost count past sixteen cups and left on an even number.

steps.title: Plates and loaves are not a problem of pairs
steps.stepSummary: רב עוירא rules that plates and loaves of bread do not carry the danger of pairs.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב עוירא said: Plates and loaves do not have the problem of pairs.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching begins. רב עוירא names some items that are not affected by the danger of pairs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the גמרא has been adding concerns about pairs. Now it starts to limit them. Two plates or two loaves on the table are not dangerous. The next step will explain why.

keyTerms.meaning: They have no issue of pairs.

phrases.english: Rav Avira said:
Plates and loaves
do not have the problem of pairs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from showing the danger to limiting where the danger of pairs applies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Plates and loaves of bread are not subject to the danger of pairs.

steps.title: The general rule: made by people versus made by Heaven
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns רב עוירא's examples into a rule. Anything finished by people is not a problem, but foods finished by Heaven are a concern.
steps.simpleTranslation: The rule of the matter: anything finished by human hands has no problem of pairs. If it was finished by Heaven, then with types of food we are concerned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רב עוירא's examples by giving one general rule behind them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A plate is made by a potter, and a loaf is baked by a baker. Both are finished by people, so pairs do not matter for them. Foods that grow on their own, finished by Heaven, still carry the concern. That fits the eggs, nuts, and cucumbers from Step 5.

keyTerms.meaning: The general rule of the matter.
By human hands, made or finished by people.

steps.confusionAlert: Bread is a food, yet it is still not a problem. What matters is who finished it, not whether you eat it. A baker finished the bread, so it falls under 'by human hands.'
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule explains why the items listed in Step 5 (eggs, nuts, cucumbers) are dangerous: they are natural foods finished by Heaven.

phrases.english: The rule of the matter:
anything whose completion was by human hands
does not have the problem of pairs.
If its completion was by Heaven,
then with types of food, we are concerned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes רב עוירא's examples and states the principle behind them.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Items finished by people are not subject to pairs. Natural foods finished by Heaven are.

steps.title: More cases with no concern of pairs: store, change of mind, guest, woman
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא lists more situations where pairs are not a concern: eating in a store, changing one's mind, being a guest, and a woman. For an important woman, we are still concerned.
steps.simpleTranslation: A store has no problem of pairs. Someone who changed his mind has no problem of pairs. A guest has no problem of pairs. A woman has no problem of pairs. But if she is an important woman, we are concerned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a list of more cases where the danger of pairs does not apply, and ends with one exception.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A store is not a person's usual place. Someone who changed his mind did not plan to drink an even number. A guest does not decide how much he gets, because the host does. The harmful forces are not particular about what a woman eats or drinks, unless she is an important woman. In that case the concern comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: One who changed his mind, for example deciding to add another cup after an odd number.
A guest eating at someone else's house.

steps.whatToRemember: The concern of pairs is real, but it is limited. It applies mainly to natural foods a person chooses to eat at home on purpose. It does not apply to things made by people, to a store, to someone who changed his mind, to a guest, or to an ordinary woman. With כשפים, it applies even to large numbers.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up this store case with the story in Step 8, where the man drank at a store and died. There the danger came from כשפים aimed at him, which is not limited this way. The store exemption here is about the general danger from מזיקין.

phrases.english: A store does not have the problem of pairs.
phrases.notes: It is not the person's regular place.

phrases.english: One who changed his mind does not have the problem of pairs.
phrases.notes: He did not plan to reach an even number.

phrases.english: A guest does not have the problem of pairs.
phrases.notes: The host decides how much he is served.

phrases.english: A woman does not have the problem of pairs.
But if she is an important woman, we are concerned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues listing limits on the danger of pairs, now based on the place, the person, and his intention rather than the item.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A store, one who changed his mind, a guest, and a woman are all exempt from the concern of pairs. An important woman is the exception, and for her we are concerned.

steps.title: The spiced drink helps but never hurts
steps.stepSummary: רב חיננא בריה דרבי יהושע rules that אִיסְפָּרָגוֹס counts toward your cups when it makes an odd number, but not when it would make an even number.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חיננא, son of רבי יהושע, said: The spiced wine drink אִיסְפָּרָגוֹס combines with your other cups for the good, but does not combine for the bad.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another rule about זוגות: a special spiced morning drink only counts when counting it helps you.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally every cup counts toward the total. אִיסְפָּרָגוֹס is different. If it brings you to an odd number, it counts and protects you. If it would bring you to an even number, it does not count, so it never creates a dangerous pair.

keyTerms.meaning: A wine drink with added spices, usually drunk in the morning
For the good (to make an odd number)
For the bad (to make an even number)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִינָּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rav Chinena, son of Rabbi Yehoshua, said:
Isparagos (spiced wine drink) combines for the good,
phrases.notes: It counts when it makes the total odd.

phrases.english: and does not combine for the bad.
phrases.notes: It does not count when it would make the total even.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִינָּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of special cases in the laws of זוגות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אִיסְפָּרָגוֹס combines to make an odd number but never to make an even number.

steps.title: What to do when unsure about pairs: two versions
steps.stepSummary: רבינא quotes רבא: if in doubt about pairs, be strict. Another version quotes רבא: if in doubt about pairs, be lenient.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said in the name of רבא: With pairs, be strict. Some report his teaching as: With pairs, be lenient.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבא's ruling for someone who is not sure if he drank an even number, and it gives two versions of what רבא said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, if you are unsure, you are strict and drink one more cup so you are not left on a pair. In the second version, you are lenient and do not drink another cup, because the extra cup might be the one that makes the pair. Both versions deal with doubt; they disagree about which action is safer.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say it (another version of the teaching)

steps.confusionAlert: The two lines are not two different rabbis arguing. They are two reports of what רבא himself said.

phrases.english: Ravina said in the name of Rava:
Pairs: be strict.
phrases.notes: If in doubt, drink another cup.

phrases.english: And some say: Pairs: be lenient.
phrases.notes: If in doubt, don't drink more, because that cup might make it even.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from which drinks count to what to do when the count is uncertain, as in the story of the man who lost count.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When unsure about pairs, one version says to drink another cup (strict); the other says not to (lenient).

steps.title: Wine joins beer, but beer does not join wine
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף rules: two cups of wine plus one of beer do not combine into three, but two cups of beer plus one of wine do combine.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Two cups of wine and one of beer do not combine. Two cups of beer and one of wine do combine.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף teaches whether different drinks join together to break a pair. He says it depends on which drink is added.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wine is the more important drink. If you drank two wines and then a beer, the weaker beer cannot join the wine, so you are still left with a pair of wine. If you drank two beers and then a wine, the stronger wine joins the beers to make three, so there is no pair.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:

phrases.aramaic: תְּרֵי דְחַמְרָא וְחַד דְּשִׁיכְרָא — לָא מִצְטָרֵף,
phrases.english: Two of wine and one of beer do not combine,
phrases.notes: The beer doesn't join, so you are left with a pair of wine.

phrases.english: two of beer and one of wine do combine.
phrases.notes: The wine joins to make three.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of which drinks combine, now with two different drinks.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The more important drink (wine) joins the weaker drink (beer), but the weaker does not join the stronger.

steps.title: A memory aid from the laws of טומאה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a way to remember רב יוסף's rule. It uses a rule from טומאה: a stricter material attached to a lesser one combines with it, but a more lenient attached material does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Your memory aid is this rule: Anything attached to it from something stricter than it is impure; from something more lenient than it is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to give a סימן, a memory hook, so you can remember which drink joins which.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the laws of טומאה, a small piece of a stricter material can join a bigger lenient object, and together they become impure. A lenient piece cannot join a stricter object in the same way. Wine works like the stricter material: it can join the beer, but beer cannot join the wine.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a proof that רב יוסף is right, and it is not a new law about drinking. It is only a memory aid that copies the same pattern.

phrases.english: And your mnemonic: This is the rule:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הַמְחוּבָּר לוֹ מִן הֶחָמוּר מִמֶּנּוּ — טָמֵא,
phrases.english: anything attached to it from that which is stricter than it is impure,
phrases.notes: The stricter piece joins, like wine joining beer.

phrases.english: from that which is more lenient than it is pure.
phrases.notes: The lenient piece doesn't join, like beer not joining wine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a memory aid for רב יוסף's rule in the previous step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The stricter thing joins the lenient one, not the other way around; this is how to remember that wine joins beer.

steps.title: Cups before the meal and cups during the meal
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן quotes רב: two cups before the meal and one during it combine. One cup before the meal and two during it do not combine.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רב: Two cups before the table and one at the table combine. One before the table and two at the table do not combine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רב's rule about whether cups drunk before the meal count together with cups drunk during the meal. In the next step, רב משרשיא challenges the second half of this rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two cups before the meal plus one during it join into three, so there is no pair. One cup before the meal plus two during it do not join, so the two cups at the meal stand alone as a dangerous pair. The cups drunk during the meal form their own group, and the earlier single cup cannot rescue them.

keyTerms.meaning: The table (on which the meal was served)
Before the table, before the meal starts
On the table, during the meal

steps.whatToRemember: Not every cup counts the same. אִיסְפָּרָגוֹס only counts for the good. Wine joins beer, but beer does not join wine. רב's rule that one cup before the meal does not join two during it is challenged by רב משרשיא in the next step.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said in the name of Rav:

phrases.aramaic: תְּרֵי קַמֵּי תַּכָּא וְחַד אַתַּכָּא — מִצְטָרְפִי.
phrases.english: Two before the table and one on the table combine.
phrases.notes: Three total, so no pair.

phrases.aramaic: חַד מִקַּמֵּי תַּכָּא וּתְרֵי אַתַּכָּא — לֹא מִצְטָרְפִין.
phrases.english: One before the table and two on the table do not combine.
phrases.notes: The two cups at the meal are a pair.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from combining different drinks to combining cups drunk at different stages of the meal.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two before the meal plus one during it combine; one before plus two during do not.

steps.title: The danger is about the person, not the table
steps.stepSummary: רב משרשיא challenges רב's ruling that one cup before the meal and two during it do not combine. The danger of pairs applies to the person, and that person has already drunk an odd number.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב משרשיא objected: Do we care about fixing the table? We care about fixing the person, and the person is already fixed.
steps.whatsHappening: רב משרשיא attacks the second half of רב's ruling from Step 16. He asks why the meal table should decide whether the cups combine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב said one cup before the meal and two during it do not combine. רב משרשיא answers that the danger of זוגות attaches to the person who drinks. That person drank three cups in total, so he should be safe no matter when the table was brought.

keyTerms.meaning: He strongly objected to it (a challenge formula)
Is it that...? (a rhetorical challenge word)
The small table set before each diner. It marks that the meal has started.
To fix or remedy (here, to protect from the danger of pairs)

phrases.english: Rav Mesharshiya objected to it:

phrases.aramaic: אַטּוּ אֲנַן לְתַקּוֹנֵי תַּכָּא קָא בָּעֵינַן?
phrases.english: Is it that we need to fix the table?
phrases.notes: He's not really asking; of course the table isn't what matters.

phrases.english: We need to fix the person,
and the person stands already fixed.
phrases.notes: He drank three cups in total, an odd number.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the second half of רב's ruling in Step 16
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that one cup before the meal and two during it do not combine
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The danger of pairs applies to the drinker, not to the meal setting. The drinker has drunk an odd number, so the cups should combine.

steps.title: Two cups at the table and one after it do not combine
steps.stepSummary: רב משרשיא gives his own rule. Everyone agrees that two cups drunk at the table and one drunk after the table is removed do not combine.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב משרשיא said: Everyone agrees that two cups at the table and one after the table do not combine.
steps.whatsHappening: Having rejected רב's version, רב משרשיא states the one case where the table does matter. This is drinking at the table and then drinking again after it is cleared.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא shows that he is replacing the earlier version with a new rule. Removing the table ends that drinking session, so a cup drunk afterward cannot join the earlier pair. The pair drunk at the table stays a pair.

keyTerms.meaning: After the table (once the table has been removed)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רב משרשיא is contradicting himself. He just said the table does not matter when drinking starts before the meal. Here he says the table does matter when it is removed, because clearing it ends the session.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Mesharshiya said:
Everyone agrees
two cups over the table and one after the table
phrases.notes: The table was removed before the third cup.

phrases.english: do not combine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב's rule after the challenge in Step 17
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two cups drunk at the table plus one drunk after the table is removed do not combine to make three.

steps.title: Support from the incident with רבה בר נחמני
steps.stepSummary: רב משרשיא supports his rule from a known incident. רבה בר נחמני had the table brought back so the drinker could drink another cup at it.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like that incident involving רבה בר נחמני.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points to a known story that supports the rule just given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In that incident, someone drank in pairs and was harmed. רבה בר נחמני had the table returned so the man could drink one more cup over it. This shows that a cup drunk after the table is removed does not fix the earlier pair. Only a cup drunk back at the table counts.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא; the incident here involves him

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הַהִיא מַעֲשֶׂה דְּרַבָּה בַּר נַחְמָנִי.
phrases.english: Like that incident of Rabba bar Naḥmani.
phrases.notes: He had the table brought back so that the extra cup would count.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הַהִיא מַעֲשֶׂה דְּרַבָּה בַּר נַחְמָנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב משרשיא's rule in Step 18
steps.raayaObject: The rule that two cups at the table and one after it do not combine
steps.raayaSupportSource: The incident where רבה בר נחמני had the table returned for an extra cup
steps.whatToRemember: The table does not matter when drinking starts before the meal (Step 17). But once the table is removed, cups drunk afterward cannot join the cups drunk at the table.

steps.title: Any diluted drink combines
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה, quoting שמואל, begins a new rule. Any diluted drink counts toward the number of cups. The statement continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: Anything diluted combines,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new rule about which kinds of drink count toward pairs. This statement is cut off and continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier steps dealt with when cups combine. This step asks which drinks count at all. שמואל's starting rule is that a diluted drink, such as wine mixed with water, counts for pairs.

keyTerms.meaning: Diluted or mixed (such as wine mixed with water)
Combines; counts toward the number of cups

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
Any diluted drink combines,
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from when cups combine to which drinks count
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any diluted drink counts toward pairs (the ruling continues on the next amud).
